problem: Prior object-goal navigation is mostly single-robot with closed-set categories, and existing multi-agent approaches rely on precomputed probabilistic graphs tied to fixed category sets, so they cannot handle novel open-vocabulary goals at test time.
motivation: Lifelong benchmarks such as GOAT-Bench require chains of open-vocabulary targets, and multiple agents could cover space faster. Pretrained VLMs and text-promptable segmenters supply zero-shot semantics and commonsense priors (e.g. microwave -> kitchen), so no retraining is needed.
key_idea: Run a decentralized multi-agent frontier-exploration system in which SAM3 gives text-prompted detection, a depth-based GoalProjector localizes goals in a shared BEV map, and a SpaceOM VLM prompt chain scores frontiers, with greedy sequential frontier allocation between agents.
insight: Multi-agent cooperation matters more than VLM reasoning in this system: on the 50-episode val_seen ablation, N=2 to N=1 drops SR from 56.2 to 38.6, while removing VLM reasoning only drops SR from 56.2 to 54.0 (modest gain, small subset, no variance reported). Failure analysis shows detection is the bottleneck for hard categories (mirror 47.6%, window glass 33.3%), and SR stays stable across subtask positions (56.1, 58.8, 55.6, 49.0), so failures do not cascade. The large SPL gap versus the end-to-end AstraNav-Memory (18.3 vs 56.9) shows the path-efficiency cost of modular frontier exploration.
method: Ego-centric BEV semantic mapping: depth is back-projected with corrected non-uniform intrinsics (f_x != f_z), transformed to geocentric coordinates and splatted into a voxel grid. Height slicing (25 cm to h_s+50 cm) gives the obstacle map, and semantic channels are projected the same way.
SAM3 open-vocabulary detection: text-prompted boxes and masks, confidence threshold 0.30, and multi-view confirmation requiring 2 consecutive detections.
GoalProjector: back-projects the SAM3 mask through calibrated depth into the BEV map and takes the centroid as the goal location, a VLM-independent localization signal.

Constraint-guided VLM frontier reasoning: SpaceOM runs a prompt chain (scene caption, room-type classification, perception gating, multi-frontier ranking) over up to K=4 frontiers to give P(g|frontier).
Bayesian value map + UCB: a per-agent value and variance map is fused with SAM3 confidence over the depth cone; frontier utility is U=(1-w)*s_vlm + w*normalized UCB, with w=0.35 and beta=1.7.

Multi-agent coordination: agent maps are fused by element-wise max-pooling into a shared global map. Frontiers are allocated by sequential greedy selection, with agent 0 choosing first and agent 1 choosing from the remainder.

FMM navigation: Fast Marching Method on the occupancy grid gives geodesic distance. A short-term goal is extracted by gradient descent and clipped to 1.25 m, then converted to discrete turn/forward actions.

setting.backbone: SAM3 (frozen) for detection/segmentation + SpaceOM VLM (frozen) for frontier scoring, with FMM planner
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (360x640 portrait, HFOV 42°, depth 0.5-5 m) + pose, per agent
setting.action_space: 6 discrete actions: STOP, forward 0.25 m, turn ±30°, turn ±10°
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D scenes, GOAT-Bench); preliminary real-drone perception-only test
setting.privileged: none stated (agent pose is given, as in the GOAT-Bench/Habitat protocol; Vicon pose in the real-world test)

numbers.extra: 2 agents; 500 steps per subtask; success radius 1.0 m; SPL for multi-agent uses max per-step displacement across agents and min distance-to-goal across agents
numbers.evidence: Table 1: GoalVLM (Ours, N=2) 0.558 / 0.183; text: 'mean DTG of 1.42 m' (Discussion also says 1.39 m)

numbers.backbone: SAM3 + GoalProjector, no SpaceOM frontier scoring

numbers_note: The paper is inconsistent: the Discussion says N=1 SR is 32.0% (vs 38.6% in Table 2) and mean DTG 1.39 m (vs 1.42 m in the results text). Ablation numbers come from a 50-episode val_seen subset, not val_unseen. The paper labels the ablation val_seen, but the text calls it a subset of the same episodes.
results: GoalVLM (N=2, zero-shot) reaches 55.8% subtask SR and 18.3% SPL on GOAT-Bench val_unseen. This beats the strongest non-end-to-end baselines, Modular GOAT (29.4/17.5) and SenseAct-NN Skill Chain (29.5/11.3), in SR, and 3D-Mem (28.8/15.8) in both. It trails the fine-tuned AstraNav-Memory (62.7 SR / 56.9 SPL), mainly on SPL.
limitations: Low path efficiency (SPL 18.3), since frontier exploration is circuitous, compared with 56.9 for learned policies
SAM3 detection fails on transparent/reflective/small objects (mirror, window glass, book, photo), and reflected depth misplaces goals
2D BEV map cannot handle multi-floor environments; real-world validation is preliminary (perception only, Vicon pose, no closed-loop navigation); ablations are on a small subset with modest VLM gain
